Hybrid ranking commonly normalizes component scores before weighted fusion: s = (1−λ)N(SASRec logits) + λN(TF-IDF similarity). Min–max normalization aligns ranges; z-score normalization aligns score spreads. Both appear in hybrid retrieval research, while Elasticsearch implements normalized weighted sums directly. For the proposed residual, |tanh(α)| ≤ 1 limits the content contribution to magnitude ≤1; whether that matters depends on SASRec score gaps near rank 10, not absolute logit values. Normalization addresses scale mismatch but does not establish calibrated relevance probabilities. Sources: [hybrid fusion research](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.290.pdf), [Elasticsearch documentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/retrievers/linear-retriever).

Suggested experiment for this benchmark: cache validation logits and title/description TF-IDF scores, inspect their spreads and rank-10 margins, then compare the baseline against a small grid of fusion weights, including zero. Select exclusively by the permitted four-category macro validation HR@10 and charge diagnostics and tuning to the search budget. Treat this as a hypothesis, not an established improvement. Guard normalization against zero variance and sparse content scores. Candidate-dependent normalization can produce different rankings for sampled candidates versus the full catalog; use a consistent reference population and identical normalization in the predictor writer and inference. Reciprocal rank fusion offers a scale-independent comparison, although it discards score-gap information. [Fusion research](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.290.pdf) discusses both normalized score fusion and rank fusion.
